title: Campania Pulls Back From Its September Fuel-Price Peak While Metano's National Rally Outpaces It
dek: Benzina and Gasolio have eased off their late-September highs across Campania, GPL is quietly climbing to new recent highs, and Metano keeps rising everywhere — just noticeably slower here than nationally.
executive_summary: As of October 13, 2026, self-service drivers in Campania are paying €2.0672/L for Benzina, €2.2887/L for Gasolio, €0.7414/L for GPL, and €1.7615/L for Metano. Benzina and Gasolio both ticked up slightly from two days earlier (October 11), by 0.06% and 0.11% respectively, while GPL and Metano held perfectly flat day-over-day. Nationally the picture was almost a mirror image: Benzina and Gasolio each dipped marginally (-0.02% and -0.04%), while GPL and Metano both edged higher. Campania remains the pricier region for liquid fuels today — Benzina running 1.01% above the national average and Gasolio 0.63% above — but it is the cheaper region for gas-based fuels, with GPL running 4.10% below the national average and Metano a full 5.91% below it.

The more interesting story sits in the seven-day averages tracked since late July. All four fuels in Campania rose from late summer into a shared peak in the week of September 21 (2026-W39), then Benzina and Gasolio turned lower — down 4.66% and 3.38% respectively from that peak through the week of October 5 — while GPL and Metano kept climbing through the same stretch. The sharpest divergence, though, is in Metano itself: since the first fully-tracked week (2026-W31, starting July 27), Metano's self-service average has risen 16.10% in Campania but 22.68% nationally — a gap of more than six and a half points that has been widening steadily week after week. Campania is not just cheaper on Metano today; the gap between it and the rest of the country has been growing for over two months.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Eases Off Its September High, and More Gently Than the National Average
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Campania closed at €2.0672/L on October 13, up a marginal 0.06% from €2.066/L two days earlier. That nudges it further above the national self-service average of €2.0465/L, a gap of 1.01% — Campania has been the pricier region for petrol for most of the tracked period, and today is no exception. Nationally, Benzina actually slipped slightly over the same two days, from €2.0468/L to €2.0465/L (-0.02%), meaning the region and the country moved in opposite directions, even if both moves were tiny.

Zoom out to the weekly averages and the real story is a round trip: Benzina in Campania rose from €1.9995/L in the week of July 27 (2026-W31) to a peak of €2.1650/L in the week of September 21 (2026-W39) — a climb of roughly 8.3% — before retreating to €2.0642/L by the week of October 5 (2026-W41), a pullback of 4.66% from the peak. Nationally the same round trip was sharper: the September 21 peak of €2.1669/L gave back 5.47% by October 5. In other words, Campania's petrol rallied slightly harder from July to September (+3.24% week-on-week vs. +2.27% nationally over the same span) but has also been pulling back a little more gently since — a small but consistent sign that this region's Benzina market is marginally stickier in both directions than the national average.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel's Retreat From a Record Tracked High Continues, Just Slower Than Nationally
paragraphs: Gasolio in Campania priced at €2.2887/L on October 13, up 0.11% from €2.2862/L on October 11 — the largest of the four day-over-day moves in either direction for the region today. That puts Campania 0.63% above the national self-service average of €2.2744/L, which itself edged down 0.04% over the same two days (from €2.2753/L). As with Benzina, the region ticked up while the country ticked down, a small divergence worth watching if it persists into next week's readings.

The multi-week picture shows diesel followed almost exactly the same arc as petrol: from €2.1532/L in the week of July 27 (2026-W31) to the tracked-period peak of €2.3638/L in the week of September 21 (2026-W39) — a rise of 9.78% — before easing back to €2.2840/L by the week of October 5 (2026-W41), down 3.38% from that peak. Nationally, diesel rose further over the same build-up (+6.80% from W31 to W41, versus Campania's +6.07%) and has also fallen further from its peak (-3.89% versus Campania's -3.38%). The pattern repeats: Campania's diesel swings are consistently a touch smaller than the national swings, in both the run-up and the pullback.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Quietly Climbs to Its Highest Level of the Tracked Period
paragraphs: GPL held flat in Campania at €0.7414/L on both October 11 and October 13 — the only fuel with zero day-over-day movement in the region. Nationally, GPL inched up 0.03% to €0.7731/L. That keeps Campania as the cheaper region for GPL by a wide margin: €0.7414/L versus €0.7731/L nationally, a 4.10% discount that has been a consistent feature of this region's gas-fuel pricing throughout the tracked period.

GPL's real story is its quiet climb off a long plateau. After bottoming around €0.7119/L in Campania through the weeks of August 31, September 14 and September 21 (2026-W36, W38 and W39), it has since risen to €0.7335/L by the week of October 5 (2026-W41) — up 3.03% off that floor — and further still to today's €0.7414/L, a cumulative 4.14% rise from the low. Nationally the same recovery has been more muted: from a floor of €0.7544/L in the week of August 31 (2026-W36) to €0.7731/L today, a 2.48% rise. Campania's GPL is cheaper in absolute terms, but it has been closing that gap faster than the national market has been moving — worth watching if the region keeps climbing at this pace.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Keeps Rising Everywhere — Just Measurably Slower in Campania
paragraphs: Metano in Campania was unchanged day-over-day, holding at €1.7615/L on both October 11 and October 13. Nationally it rose 0.29%, from €1.8667/L to €1.8721/L — the largest single day-over-day move of any fuel nationally today. That widens Campania's discount on Metano to 5.91% below the national average, the single biggest regional-versus-national gap of any of the four fuels tracked.

This is also where the clearest trend divergence in today's data lives: Metano has risen every single tracked week since the week of July 27 (2026-W31) with no pullback at all, in both Campania and nationally — but at very different speeds. Campania's self-service average has gone from €1.5129/L to today's €1.7615/L, a rise of 16.43%. Nationally, the same fuel has gone from €1.5175/L to €1.8721/L, a rise of 23.37%. That's a gap of nearly seven percentage points that has opened up gradually, week after week, since late July — Campania is not just cheaper on Metano, it is also rising more slowly, and the gap between the two has not closed once in the eleven weeks of data collected so far.

network_section.heading: Station Coverage Dips Slightly as Campania's Reporting Rate Trails the National Average
paragraphs: Campania has 2,118 registered stations as of today, with 1,844 of them reporting a price today — a reporting rate of 87.06%. That's down slightly from 87.29% two days ago (1,848 of 2,117 registered stations reporting on October 11), a small dip worth noting but not yet a trend on its own.

Nationally, 21,631 of 23,929 registered stations reported today, a reporting rate of 90.40% — meaning Campania's network is reporting at a rate roughly 3.3 points below the national average. A lower reporting rate doesn't change the prices shown here (which are averaged only over stations that did report), but it's a useful caveat: Campania's daily figures rest on a slightly smaller share of its total station network than the national figures do.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made: Zero Manual Steps, Every Single Day
paragraphs: Every part of this report — the underlying price and station data, the region-of-the-day rotation, the week-by-week trend analysis, and the prose itself — is produced automatically each morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. The pipeline pulls the latest MIMIT fuel-price and station-registry feeds, recomputes national and regional weekly averages, deterministically rotates through all twenty of Italy's regions so each one gets its turn in the spotlight, and then has an AI model read the resulting numbers and write up what changed and why it matters — all before a human has looked at a single row of data.

That stands in sharp contrast to the traditional approach to this kind of tracking: a manually-maintained spreadsheet, updated by hand whenever someone remembers to download the latest CSV, with charts that have to be rebuilt and commentary that has to be rewritten from scratch every time. This report is generated, checked against source figures, and published the same way every day — which is also why every number cited above is pulled directly from the day's dataset rather than estimated or carried over from a previous write-up.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Agip Eni's Brand View
paragraphs: The live Fuel Dashboard opens by default on Agip Eni's brand-level view, but that's just the starting point. Use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality, or any other Operator/Brand to see how prices and trends compare across the rest of Italy's fuel market — including today's featured region, Campania, and the national trends referenced throughout this report.

pull_quote: Metano has climbed 23.37% nationally since late July — but in Campania the same fuel has risen only 16.43%, a gap that has widened every single week for eleven straight weeks.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Campania. Benzina and Gasolio here have both pulled back from their late-September peak, while GPL just quietly touched its highest point of the whole tracked period and Metano keeps climbing nationwide — just noticeably slower in Campania than anywhere else. Since late July, Metano is up 23.4% across Italy but only 16.4% in Campania, a gap that has widened every week for eleven weeks straight.

Fuel Dashboard tracks self-service and served prices for Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano across every Italian region, province, municipality and fuel brand, updated daily from the official MIMIT feed. You can explore it yourself at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/.

What I find genuinely interesting about this project isn't the fuel prices themselves — it's that the entire thing, including this write-up, runs without me touching a spreadsheet. A pipeline built with Claude Code pulls the data, computes the regional and national trends, picks a new region to spotlight each day, and drafts the analysis you just read, every single morning, unattended. A few years ago this would have been a recurring manual Excel chore. Today it's a self-updating dashboard and report that a small AI-assisted pipeline maintains on its own. That shift — from manually-updated spreadsheets to interactive, self-maintaining dashboards — is available to far more people than most realize.
